title: Reverse Linked List
keyIdea: Walk once with prev / curr / next: save next, point curr->next back to prev, move prev and curr forward. When curr is NULL, prev is the new head.

approaches.name: Recursion
approaches.idea: Reverse everything after head (returns the new head), then head->next->next = head and head->next = NULL.
approaches.why: One call per node on the call stack.

approaches.name: Three pointers (iterative)
approaches.idea: prev = NULL, curr = head. Loop: next = curr->next; curr->next = prev; prev = curr; curr = next. Return prev.
approaches.why: Each node's pointer is flipped once; only three extra pointers.

quiz.q: Why save next before curr->next = prev?
options: After the flip, curr no longer points to the rest of the list, so it would be lost

quiz.q: Why return prev and not curr?
options: The loop ends when curr is NULL; prev holds the old last node, the new head
prev is always the old head

quiz.q: In the recursive version, what does head->next->next = head do?
options: The old next node is now the tail of the reversed part; it points back to head

quiz.q: Why is head->next = NULL needed in the recursive version?
options: head is the new tail; otherwise head and its old next would point at each other (a cycle)
